attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The paraphrase follows the wording. But the sentence is a polemical bundle ('death of the art of technology', 'by definition', 'by design', 'financially ruinous') with no metric, population, comparator or period. It works as rhetoric, not as a testable observation.

contract.note: The evaluator supplies the April–June 2025 period, the net-workload comparator, the per-task efficiency measure and a financial test, and the speaker named none of these. The financially harmed entity is never identified. The result would depend on these choices, not on the speaker's words.

evidence.note: A METR randomized study of early-2025 tools in one setting. It measures task duration, not cognitive load, and covers only a narrow population. Context only.
A small preprint finding reduced workload on some Copilot tasks. It cuts against a universal 'adds load' claim but is narrow and not dated to the period. Context.

reviews.rationale: This is a sweeping evaluative characterisation that combines rhetoric with vague assertions: 'by definition' and 'by design', and financial ruin for an unnamed party. It sets no measurable standard, so the evaluator would have to invent one. The packet only has narrow studies pointing in different directions. Not adjudicable as stated.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: In context, 'this path' means gains coming from burning more tokens. 'No changing this path' is a firm, unhedged claim that it cannot change, with no deadline. 'Out of ideas' is rhetorical colour.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'capability gains require more generated tokens' follows the preceding sentence ('all the gains... come from burning more and more tokens'). Counting a public successor that scores higher with fewer tokens as a counterexample is a fair, ordinary test.

evidence.note: Independent benchmarking dated 2025-09-25, after the post: in reasoning mode, the updated Flash and Flash-Lite score higher on the same index while using 24% and 50% fewer output tokens.
Google's own disclosure confirming the public release that day and the fewer-tokens claim. It corroborates e1 but is not independent.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met. On 2025-09-25, a month after the post, publicly released Gemini 2.5 Flash and Flash-Lite updates scored higher on an independent evaluation than their predecessors while using fewer output tokens in reasoning mode. That contradicts the claim that improvement cannot leave the more-tokens path.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A categorical retrospective claim ('the only way... have been able to') about how developers improved new models up to the time of the post.

contract.note: 'Only' is the speaker's own word, so a single meaningful improvement in a recent non-reasoning model is a fair counterexample. The period ending at publication matches 'have been able to'.

evidence.note: OpenAI's GPT-4.5 release (Feb 2025) describes a non-reasoning model improved by scaling unsupervised learning, e.g. GPQA 71.4% vs 53.6% for GPT-4o. It is a company disclosure, but it is a primary model report as the contract requires.

reviews.rationale: Before the post, GPT-4.5 was released as a model that does not reason before answering. Its primary report shows clear benchmark gains over GPT-4o that came from scaling pre-training, not from inference-time reasoning. That is a counterexample to 'the only way'. The scores are self-reported, but they are on standard public benchmarks.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim that well-resourced generative AI companies have no product with a defined, meaningful mass-market use case. The resource premise is qualitative.

contract.note: The plain reading (an identifiable practical use with broad recurring adoption) is an ordinary reading of 'defined... mass-market use case'. 'Meaningful' is partly evaluative, and the speaker might mean economic significance, but the reading is not stretched against him.

evidence.note: An NBER working paper that includes OpenAI-employed authors and uses company data. It reports about 10% of the world's adults using the product by July 2025, with practical guidance, information seeking and writing making up nearly 80% of use. Not independent.
OpenAI's own summary of the same study. A company disclosure that adds no independent corroboration.

reviews.rationale: By July 2025, ChatGPT had broad recurring consumer adoption (about 10% of the world's adults), mostly for identifiable practical tasks such as writing and information seeking. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. Caveat: the measurement comes from company data, which the contract allows as disclosed active-user measurement with methods.
